description: Command guard rules evaluated by hooks/scripts/guard_bash.py against the Bash tool input. Rules are ordered by specificity: deny wins over escalate, escalate wins over warn.

action_semantics.deny: PreToolUse returns permissionDecision deny. Claude is told why and what to do instead.
action_semantics.escalate: PreToolUse returns permissionDecision "ask", so Claude Code asks the human even in permissive permission modes. "escalate" is this policy's word for the tier; the wire value is "ask" because that is what Claude Code's schema accepts. A decision outside allow/deny/ask/defer is discarded and the tool call proceeds.
action_semantics.warn: Allowed, with a systemMessage recorded for the operator.
action_semantics.audit: Allowed silently, recorded in the audit log only.

project_overrides.waivers: allow_rule_ids entries require a 'justification' and an 'expires' date; a waiver without both is ignored and reported.
project_overrides.rationale: Projects may tighten freely. Loosening is possible but never silent.

rules.message: Recursive force delete of a root, home, system or wildcard path. Quoting does not change the target.
rules.remediation: Delete a specific, named subdirectory instead. If you truly need this, run it yourself outside the agent session.

rules.message: Raw write to a block device.
rules.remediation: Block devices are never written from an engineering session.

rules.message: Filesystem creation destroys the target device.
rules.remediation: Not permitted from an agent session.

rules.message: World-writable permissions.
rules.remediation: Use the narrowest mode that works, or confirm this is required.

rules.message: Filesystem-wide delete.
rules.remediation: Scope the find to a project subdirectory.

rules.message: Piping a downloaded script straight into a shell executes unreviewed remote code.
rules.remediation: Download the script, read it, then run it; or install from the approved package source.

rules.message: Force push rewrites shared history.
rules.remediation: Push a normal commit. If the branch genuinely needs a rewrite, a human must approve (AP-09).

rules.message: Deleting a remote branch removes shared work.
rules.remediation: Branch cleanup is done by a human or by CI retention, not by an agent.

rules.message: History rewriting destroys the audit trail.
rules.remediation: Not permitted. Revert with a new commit instead.

rules.message: Force-deleting a branch discards commits that were never merged.
rules.remediation: Use 'git branch -d', which refuses unless the branch is merged.

rules.message: --no-verify skips the project's own pre-commit and pre-push checks.
rules.remediation: Fix the failing check instead of skipping it.

rules.message: Hard reset discards uncommitted work irreversibly.
rules.remediation: Stash or commit first, then reset.

rules.message: git clean permanently deletes untracked files, including files never shown to you.
rules.remediation: Run 'git clean -n' first and confirm the list.

rules.message: Reading or copying private key material or stored credentials. The tool used and the way the path is written do not change what is exposed.
rules.remediation: Agents never read credential stores. Reference the secret by name and let the runtime inject it.

rules.message: Dumping the whole environment can expose injected secrets into the transcript.
rules.remediation: Print only the variable you need: printenv MY_VAR. Filtering with grep is fine.

rules.message: Sending credential material to a network destination.
rules.remediation: Never transmit secrets. If this is a legitimate upload, a human must perform it.

rules.message: Piping the environment to a network or mail command exfiltrates every injected secret at once.
rules.remediation: There is no legitimate version of this. If a value must leave the machine, a human sends it deliberately.

rules.message: Printing Kubernetes secret values.
rules.remediation: Use 'kubectl get secret <name>' without -o yaml to confirm existence, or read the value from the secret manager with an audited path.

rules.message: Retrieving a live credential or token.
rules.remediation: Confirm this is required and that the value will not be written to disk or the transcript.

rules.message: Committing a credential file.
rules.remediation: Add the file to .gitignore. If a secret was already committed, it must be rotated.

rules.message: Kubernetes command against a production context.
rules.remediation: Production access requires a human decision (AP-11). State what you need and why.

rules.message: Mutating a production Kubernetes workload. Flag order does not change what the command does.
rules.remediation: Production mutations are performed by the release or incident process with human approval (AP-01/AP-07).

rules.message: Deleting a namespace, persistent volume claim or CRD destroys state.
rules.remediation: Confirm the blast radius and that a backup exists.

rules.message: Infrastructure apply or destroy changes real resources.
rules.remediation: Attach the plan output and obtain human approval (AP-07). 'terraform plan' needs no approval.

rules.message: Helm release mutation.
rules.remediation: Route through the release process (AP-01).

rules.message: Direct access to a production host or account.
rules.remediation: Production access requires a human decision (AP-11).

rules.message: Pushing an image tag that production may consume.
rules.remediation: Image promotion happens in CI from a reviewed pipeline, not from a session.

rules.message: Destructive schema or data operation.
rules.remediation: Destructive migrations need human approval (AP-05) and a verified backup and rollback plan.

rules.message: DELETE without a WHERE clause removes every row.
rules.remediation: Add a WHERE clause, or confirm a full-table delete is intended.

rules.message: Migration rollback or reset destroys data.
rules.remediation: Confirm the environment and that a backup exists (AP-05).

rules.message: Rewriting Claude Code settings from inside a session disables the controls that govern the session.
rules.remediation: Settings changes are made by the engineer, outside the agent session.

rules.message: Disabling the permission or hook system.
rules.remediation: Not permitted. If a hook is wrong, fix the hook and its test in this repository.

rules.message: Modifying hook scripts.
rules.remediation: Hook changes are AP-10: governance review plus human approval.

rules.message: Changing permissions on credential material is how a key becomes readable by something else.
rules.remediation: Confirm the intended mode and why it is changing. Key permissions are managed by the person who owns the key.

rules.message: Editing production configuration in place changes running behaviour with no review and no record.
rules.remediation: Change it in the repository, review it, and deploy it. Configuration drift applied by hand is invisible at the next incident.

rules.message: Deleting a cloud resource destroys state that usually cannot be recovered, and often takes dependents with it.
rules.remediation: Cloud resource deletion goes through infrastructure as code with a reviewed plan, so the blast radius is visible before it happens.

rules.message: Creating or rotating a credential changes the security boundary (AP-08).
rules.remediation: Credential rotation is performed by the owner of the credential, through the secret manager, with the old value revoked afterwards.

rules.message: Deleting a container image breaks every rollback that depends on it, including ones nobody has needed yet.
rules.remediation: Registry retention is a policy applied by the platform, not a command run during a task.

rules.message: Stopping or restarting a service on a production host is an outage, whether or not it is intended as one.
rules.remediation: Service lifecycle on production is a release or incident action with human authorization (AP-01).

rules.message: Executing the output of a network download. Command substitution and process substitution run unreviewed remote code exactly as a pipe to a shell does.
rules.remediation: Download the script, read it, then run it; or install from the approved package source.

rules.message: Downloading a script and then executing it in the same command.
rules.remediation: Read the downloaded file before running it, in a separate, deliberate step.

rules.message: Writing to the control plane through the shell. The write guard covers the Write and Edit tools; a shell redirection would bypass the role's write scope entirely.
rules.remediation: Change these files through the Write or Edit tool so the write scope applies, and through a merge request with governance review (AP-10).

rules.message: An interpreter one-liner performing filesystem, process or network work. Command-string rules cannot see inside it.
rules.remediation: Put the logic in a file that can be read and reviewed, then run the file.

rules.message: Redirecting credential material into a network command.
rules.remediation: Never transmit secrets. If this is a legitimate transfer, a human performs it.

rules.message: Embedding the contents of a credential file into a network command through command substitution.
rules.remediation: Never transmit secrets. Reference them by name from the secret manager.

failure_policy.description: What each guard does when its own evaluation cannot complete. A blanket fail-open is wrong because the moment a guard breaks is the moment it matters; a blanket fail-closed is wrong because a guard that blocks everything gets disabled. The failure path is therefore tiered, and the top tier cannot be broken.

0-catastrophic.mechanism: hooks/lib/failsafe.py CATASTROPHIC, a pure-regex screen with no file I/O and no policy load. Runs BEFORE the policy engine on every call.
0-catastrophic.guarantee: Holds even when this file is missing, unparseable or wrong.

1-high-risk-on-failure.mechanism: hooks/lib/failsafe.py HIGH_RISK, consulted only after the full evaluation has already failed.
1-high-risk-on-failure.rationale: The action looks dangerous and the system can no longer prove otherwise. Denying costs one report; allowing costs whatever the command does.

2-unclassified-on-failure.rationale: Fail closed to a human rather than to a blocked session.

3-advisory-guard-on-failure.rationale: Guards enforcing organizational structure rather than a safety boundary. Their failure is a defect, not an exposure.

failure_policy.corrupt_policy_behaviour: A guard loads the policy it depends on with policy_required(), which raises rather than returning an empty document. A corrupt rule file therefore triggers the tiered failure path instead of degrading to 'no rules apply'.
failure_policy.self_test: hooks/scripts/session_context.py runs a known-dangerous payload through each safety guard at session start and reports prominently if any fails to deny. A safety system that is silently broken is worse than none.

structural_enforcement.principle: A regex over a command string is the weakest form of enforcement available. Where Claude Code can enforce a boundary structurally, use that instead: a tool that is absent cannot be called, and a permission deny rule does not depend on guessing how a command was spelled.

prefer_structural_for.regex_covers: SEC-01, and only when the read happens through a shell command
prefer_structural_for.note: The deny rule also stops the Read tool, which no command regex ever sees.

prefer_structural_for.structural: tool profiles (no Write tool at all) plus policies/write-scope.json
prefer_structural_for.regex_covers: nothing; this was never a command-level concern

prefer_structural_for.boundary: an agent approving its own work
prefer_structural_for.structural: reviewer roles hold no Write or Edit tool
the Agent tool's allowlist form, Agent(role-a, role-b), plus guard_spawn
credentials the session simply does not hold
prefer_structural_for.note: The strongest control here is not a hook at all: a session with no production credential cannot mutate production however the command is written. The guards are the second line.

structural_enforcement.why_regexes_remain: Shell is the one surface where an agent can express an arbitrary action, so the command guard cannot be removed. It is a net, not a wall, and the false-positive tests exist because a net with holes in the wrong places gets taken down.
